beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The Museum of Good Reasons makes true explanations unsettling by showing what they leave outside.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This philosophical novel follows Mara, hired to catalogue a museum that justifies disappearance.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Her first test concerns a lamp described as creating light from darkness.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: She notices the oil that the label places outside the exhibit.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The director asks where her own explanation chooses to stop.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That exchange invites readers to examine framing without pretending complete descriptions are possible.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An apparently generous umbrella becomes another test of what official language permits.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Mara reads two accounts of the same walk through rainy streets.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: One describes offered companionship; the other describes repeated attempts to leave.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Her work includes physically retracing the route from each person’s position.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The novel makes perspective a material experience, not merely a contest between persuasive sentences.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A moved park bench has better shade and still supports sitting.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The official reply uses those facts to answer a widower’s complaint.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: But his wife’s death there made its location matter.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Mara cannot correct the reply simply by finding a false statement.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The scene shows why this novel gives ordinary objects histories worth following.
